question: Does raising the toolchain from Rust 1.98.1 to 1.99.1, and updating the locked dependencies with it, change anything the tool reports or delivers?
method: Three release binaries of oadec-cli (`cargo build --release --locked -p oadec-cli`): main at 0.8.0 with rustc 1.98.1 (48a229cea 2026-09-01); the same sources with rustc 1.99.1 (58cf8f9c3 2026-10-13); and those sources with the updated locks. The streams are the 125 of the work directory and the repository: 41 raw TrueHD streams (one whole film and forty 60-second heads of library titles), 56 AC-3 and E-AC-3 heads, 18 clips and the 10 committed fixtures. The toolchain step alone was compared with tools/old_new.py --decode: exit codes, every field of `verify --json` and `info --json`, every line of `verify`, and the PCM of presentation 2 of every TrueHD and MLP stream. The first binary and the last were then compared with the --decode-all mode tools/old_new.py gains in the pull request after this one, which runs every delivery with both binaries into a directory of its own and hashes every file found there: `decode -p 0..3 --format pcm` for TrueHD and MLP, `decode --format pcm` with and without `--core-only` for AC-3 and E-AC-3, and `--format damf` and `--format adm` for all.

locks.workspace: 17 packages, patch releases all: bit-vec 0.10.2, clap 4.6.7 with clap_builder, clap_derive and clap_lex, itoa 1.0.19, libc 0.2.191, log 0.4.35, rustix 1.1.6, serde_json 1.0.154, syn 3.0.10, thiserror 2.0.21 with thiserror-impl, toml_datetime 1.1.3, toml_edit 0.25.19, unicode-ident 1.0.27, winnow 1.0.5
locks.adm_audit_harness: 6 packages: itoa, serde_json, syn, thiserror, thiserror-impl, unicode-ident, to the same versions

checks_on_the_final_state.cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -: clean; the new toolchain raises no lint the old one did not
checks_on_the_final_state.cargo deny check: advisories ok, bans ok, licenses ok, sources ok
checks_on_the_final_state.cargo deny check on the harness manifest: failed on the harness itself, which named no licence, before and after the update; ok once it does

reading: Nothing moved. The compiler and the seventeen patch releases leave every exit code, every reported field, every line of `verify` and every delivered byte where they were, on 90.6 GB of output: integer PCM, the floating point of the AC-3 family, and both object formats. That the floating-point outputs are identical across two compiler releases on one machine says nothing about another platform's mathematics library. An exit code of 2 in a delivery row is a refusal, the same from both binaries: a presentation the stream does not carry, or an object format asked of a stream with no object programme.
